### About

This site is designed to find the set of bikes that match the specifications you want in a frame. The focus is frame geometry, but there are also filters for material, suspension correction, UDH compatability, sliding dropout, handlebar (flat or drop), axle spacing, and maximum tire width.

### Gravel style

This site classifies bikes into Racy, Relaxed, and Rowdy styles based on their frame geometry.

* Racy bikes are racy!
* Relaxed bikes are generally designed for long tours or exploring off road
* Rowdy bikes are mountainy bikey

This is somewhat unique -- most websites or podcasts that I know of categorize gravel bikes as "more racy" or "more mountain bikey"

### Things to do here:

[Which bikes are racy/rowdy/relaxed?](qmd/gravel_mds.qmd) -- Compare overall similarity of frame geometry among hundreds of gravel bikes, color coded by style. This is the page with the filters.

What makes a [racy frame racy?](qmd/what_makes_a_racy_bike_racy.qmd), a [relaxed frame relaxed?](qmd/what_makes_a_relaxed_bike_relaxed.qmd), and a [rowdy frame rowdy?](qmd/what_makes_a_rowdy_bike_rowdy.qmd) - plots showing which frame measures are most correlated with a style, and which aren't.

The [Gravel 2D](qmd/gravel_scatter.qmd) page contains interactive, 2D scatter plots of different pairs of frame geometry measures for all gravel bike models and frame sizes in the database.

### How does my bike frame geometry change if I add suspension

See how your bike frame's [geometry changes with a suspension fork](qmd/gravel_sus_fork.qmd).

See how your bike frame's [relative similarity to other bikes changes with a suspension fork]( qmd/gravel_scatter_sus.qmd).


### The classification

The [Gravel Tree](qmd/gravel_tree.qmd) page contains a tree diagram showing the relative similarity in frame geometry among all gravel bikes in the database and the clustering of the models into three major styles.


The [Gravel Table](qmd/gravel_class.qmd) page contains a table of the classification of all gravel bike models in the database into All-road, Endurance, and Trail categories.
